value.rationale: For a natural infinitely divisible Gaussian-plus-rare-jumps model, the best variance-constrained Bernstein scale is a meaningful quantitative tail descriptor. A known generic leading-order inverse logarithm cannot distinguish different bounded jump laws, whereas the newly derived beta-dependent coefficient and tail-amplitude constant identify how jump endpoint regularity alters the exact optimum. It is an entire regular-variation class with a nontrivial global saddle argument, not an arbitrary fixed-value calculation; it does not require downstream claims.
